title: Mod Scenario Header
description: The required header file for a split mod scenario (scenario.json). Must contain scenarioId. May also embed domain arrays for simple mods that don't need separate files.

scenarioId.description: Unique identifier for this scenario, e.g. 'my_mod.my_scenario'

displayName.description: Human-readable display name shown in the scenario picker

startYear.description: Year the scenario begins. Historical mods are free to start centuries before the base game's 2026.

startTick.description: Absolute game tick to start at. 0 = derive from year/month/day.

clearDiplomaticRelationships.description: Wipe all diplomatic relationships before applying scenario state

clearDiplomacyScope.description: Which relationships to clear: 'core' = wars/alliances only; 'extended' = all

rebuildNeutralRelations.description: Re-initialise neutral opinion modifiers after clearing relationships

provinceDataFile.description: Per-province population, terrain and latent resources, relative to the scenario folder (scenario/provinces_data.json). Applied when a new game starts; terrain and resources are re-applied on every load.

nationalGoalsFile.description: National goals file, relative to the scenario folder, in the national_goals_2026.json shape ({ "_BASIC": { "goals": [...] }, "OTT": { "goals": [...] } }). It REPLACES the base goals for the Agenda panel and the AI; a file without _BASIC means no starter goals.

victoryFile.description: Victory file, relative to the scenario folder (see mod_scenario_victory.schema.json): the scenario's own endings (mod_victories), extra end-screen rows (end_screen_rows) and the switch that turns the five base victories off (disable_base_victories). Checked once a month; the first ending whose conditions hold ends the game. The Mod Builder's Endings tab edits it.

gdpScale.description: Multiplies every country's GDP, GDP per capita, exports, imports, foreign reserves, treasury and opening monthly budgets (revenue, expenses, defense, research) once, when a new game starts. Tutorial treasury rewards are paid times this scale too, capped at economy.max_single_event_treasury_gdp_fraction of the player's GDP (5%, the cap event treasury effects get). countryStateOverrides values are absolute and are applied after it; a country whose gdp is overridden has its opening monthly budgets and its trade (exports, imports and the tariff and commercial-hub revenue they bring) re-based on that GDP.

unownedProvincePopulationScale.description: Multiplies the population of every province that is still unowned after removeCountries and the ownership overrides, once, when a new game starts. Provinces are baked with 2026 headcounts, and unowned land brings them back when it is colonised; a historical scenario sets this to roughly its declared world population divided by the 2026 population of the provinces its countries own. A scaled province keeps at least 100 people (or its own population, if smaller). 1 or omitted leaves unowned provinces alone. Owned provinces follow each country's declared population instead.

economicEraLabel.description: Label key for the economic era, used by the economy init system

disabledUnitCategories.description: Unit categories removed from availability, recruitment UI, and build eligibility for the whole scenario.

disabledUnitTypeIds.description: Specific unit type ids removed from availability, recruitment UI, and build eligibility for the whole scenario.

restrictOwnersToOwnedUnits.description: A unit type with an ownerIso3 is exclusive to that country. When true, a country that owns unit types may recruit ONLY those (a historical scenario giving each nation its own roster). When false, owners keep every other available unit too.

disabledBuildingCategories.description: Building categories removed from every build menu, starting seeding, the AI and the build command for the whole scenario.

disabledBuildingIds.description: Specific building ids removed from every build menu, starting seeding, the AI and the build command for the whole scenario. To drop most of the base roster, prefer "mode": "replace" in a buildings override file.

disabledDoctrineBranches.description: Knowledge Network branches hidden from the research screen and never researched. Their tier gates never open, so every building, unit and law gated behind them stays locked.

buildingsOverrideFile.description: Path, relative to the scenario folder, of a buildings override file (same shape as a mod's Content/buildings.json, see mod_content_envelope.schema.json). Applied after every mod's Content/buildings.json; "mode": "replace" makes it the whole roster.

unitsOverrideFile.description: Path, relative to the scenario folder, of a units override file (see mod_content_envelope.schema.json). Applied after every mod's Content/units.json.

resourcesOverrideFile.description: Path, relative to the scenario folder, of a resources override file (see mod_content_envelope.schema.json). Resources are a fixed set: they can be re-priced, re-skinned or disabled, not added.

techOverrideFile.description: Deprecated and ignored: the tech tree was replaced by the Knowledge Network doctrines. Rewrite doctrine cards in overrides/doctrines.json and hide branches with disabledDoctrineBranches.

currencySymbol.description: Money symbol shown everywhere when no currencies file assigns a national currency (default "$").

currenciesFile.description: Path, relative to the scenario folder, of a currencies file (see mod_currencies.schema.json). Stacked on top of the active mods' Content/currencies.json. Display-only.

worldCeasefire.description: A world ceasefire the scenario starts with. It suspends the wars running between the covered countries (no battles, sieges, occupation progress, war score or exhaustion growth, air strikes, blockades or nuclear launches, and armies cannot enter each other's land; participants, occupations and peace terms stay) and refuses new declarations of war between them. The scenario's own starting wars are declared first and then suspended, so a scenario can open mid-war with the guns silent. Peace deals stay possible. Events can also start and end one (start_world_ceasefire / end_world_ceasefire).

startDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD, counted with the game's 30-day months. The day the ceasefire begins; blank = the scenario's first day.

endDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD. The ceasefire ends on this day; blank = no end date (it then ends by untilFlag or an end_world_ceasefire effect only).

untilFlag.description: The ceasefire also ends the moment any country holds the event flag with this name (set by a set_flag effect). Blank = no flag ends it.

countries.description: ISO3 codes the ceasefire covers. A pair of countries is covered only when BOTH are listed. Empty = every country.

blockDeclarations.description: True: a declaration of war between covered countries is refused while the ceasefire holds (a declare_war effect with force: true still goes through, and that war stays live).

suspendWars.description: True: the wars running between covered countries are suspended while the ceasefire holds.
